articles.headline: No. 16 Washington women beat Stanford 105-50, the Cardinal's worst loss in program history
articles.description: — Brynn McGaughy scored a career-high 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 points on 7-of-10 shooting and No. 16 Washington handed Stanford its worst loss in program history, beating the Cardinal 105-50 on Friday night.

article.story: ATLANTA -- — Skylar Forbes had 23 points, Gia Cooke scored 20 and No. 24 West Virginia rolled to an 81-63 victory over Georgia Tech on Sunday. Forbes made 8 of 21 shots, including 3 of 10 from 3-point range, for the Mountaineers (3-0). Cooke shot 6 for 14, sinking 3 of 4 from distance and 5 of 6 at the free-throw line. Kennedy Harris also hit 3 of 4 from distance and scored 11 for West Virginia. Khyala Ngodu pitched in with nine points and 10 rebounds. Talayah Walker had 21 points on 7-for-20 shooting for the Yellow Jackets (2-1). Ariadna Termis scored 14. Cooke had nine points and Harris hit two 3-pointers and scored eight to guide West Virginia to a 27-16 lead after one quarter. Forbes had seven points in the second and the Mountaineers cruised into halftime with a 43-30 advantage. West Virginia outrebounded Georgia Tech 19-10 before the break and turned nine offensive boards into 16 second-chance points. Forbes scored half of West Virginia's 24 points in the third and the lead grew to 67-45 heading to the fourth. West Virginia shot 48% from the floor — to Georgia Tech's 42% — and won the battle of the boards 37-28 with 14 coming at the offensive end, leading to 23 second-chance points. The Mountaineers outscored the Yellow Jackets 42-26 in the paint. Up next West Virginia: Hosts Northwestern on Friday.
